title: Port to Temporal v1.31.2 (epic)
content: Epic tracking the full port of temporal-yugabyte's CustomDataStore from Temporal v1.29.7 to v1.31.2. See [[s-2kt2]] for the full design/context. Closes when all child issues close and the acceptance criteria in [[s-2kt2]] are met.

title: Bump go.mod to v1.31.2
content:
Foundation issue — bump `go.temporal.io/server` to `v1.31.2` and `go.temporal.io/api` in lockstep (upstream pins `v1.62.8`; this project currently pins `v1.53.0`). Verify the go directive vs. upstream's `1.26.4`; check `github.com/temporalio/cli` and `github.com/temporalio/ui-server/v2` for symbol conflicts (cli depends on `go.temporal.io/server v1.29.1` but is only used for the `cmd/tools/cli` shim, not linked into the server binary's persistence path).

Expected to leave the build broken until [[i-serializer-injection]] and [[i-chasm-routing]] land — track as a single feature branch, not a mergeable increment on its own.

Implements [[s-88l3]]. Blocks every other issue in this epic — nothing else can be verified against the new interfaces until this lands.

feedback.content:
**Implemented:** `go.temporal.io/server` → `v1.31.2`, `go.temporal.io/api` → `v1.62.8` (lockstep, as planned). `go get` auto-bumped the go directive `1.26.0` → `1.26.4` to satisfy upstream's own directive. `go mod tidy` is clean.

**Deviation from spec — bigger issue than anticipated:** the spec only flagged "check `github.com/temporalio/cli` for symbol conflicts." The actual finding was worse: `github.com/temporalio/cli` moved its `temporalcli` package to `internal/temporalcli` somewhere between v1.5.2 and v1.6.0, so the public Go API this project's `cmd/tools/cli/main.go` wrapped (`temporalcli.Execute(...)`) no longer exists for any cli version compatible with server v1.31.x. Resolution:
- Bumped `github.com/temporalio/cli` to `v1.8.2`, the first stable tag pinning `go.temporal.io/server v1.31.2` exactly.
- That version also split out `github.com/temporalio/cli/cliext` as a separate git-subdirectory pseudo-module, resolved only via a local `replace github.com/temporalio/cli/cliext => github.com/temporalio/cli/cliext v0.0.0-20260731000218-c579925f193f` pinned to the exact commit tagged `v1.8.2` (their own go.mod uses a `replace ... => ./cliext` local-path replace that only applies within their module, not to consumers — this had to be re-derived here).
- **Deleted `cmd/tools/cli/main.go`** — it was a byte-for-byte copy of upstream's old `cmd/temporal/main.go`, which no longer compiles externally. Upstream's own `cmd/temporal/main.go` is now functionally identical (imports the same now-internal package from within their module, where `internal/` is legal). Rather than re-vendor a wrapper, the Makefile's `target/temporal` rule now builds `github.com/temporalio/cli/cmd/temporal` directly as a Go **tool dependency** (`go get -tool github.com/temporalio/cli/cmd/temporal`, Go 1.24+ `tool` directive in go.mod) — this is the only way to keep a package required in go.mod/go.sum without any local `.go` file importing it, since `go mod tidy` would otherwise drop it as unused.
- Verified: `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /tmp/t github.com/temporalio/cli/cmd/temporal && /tmp/t --version` → `temporal version 0.0.0-DEV (Server 1.31.2, UI 2.50.1)`.

**Evidence:** `go mod tidy` exits clean. `go build ./...` now fails *only* with the 10 errors already anticipated and scoped to sibling issues (all in `driver/`: missing `GetHistoryBranchUtil`, removed `serialization.*` free functions) — i-1fxp (serializer injection) and i-1myt (archetype routing) own those. No errors outside `driver/`; `cmd/server`'s own renamed-API issues (i-5y8n) can't be confirmed yet since `cmd/server` imports the still-broken `driver` package — expected, will surface once i-1fxp/i-1myt close.

**Files touched:** `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `Makefile` (one build rule), deleted `cmd/tools/cli/main.go`.

title: Serializer injection through factory and stores
content:
Thread `serialization.Serializer` from `MetaFactory.NewFactory`/`InstanceFactory` down to every store constructor in `driver/`, per the new upstream `AbstractDataStoreFactory.NewFactory` signature. Fix call sites that used now-removed `serialization.*` free functions, switch `HistoryStore` to embed `p.HistoryBranchUtil` (interface) via `p.NewHistoryBranchUtil(serializer)` instead of the old `p.HistoryBranchUtilImpl{}` value embed.

Full design: [[s-28q1]].

Blocked by the go.mod bump. Blocks [[i-chasm-routing]] (needs the new `NewMutableStateStore` signature) and [[i-test-harness]] (exercises the new constructor signatures).

feedback.content:
**Implemented per spec, one deliberate deviation:**
- `driver/factory.go`: `MetaFactory.NewFactory`/`NewFactoryFromSession` gained trailing `serializer serialization.Serializer` (matches the new `AbstractDataStoreFactory.NewFactory` signature exactly); `InstanceFactory` carries it and passes it to `NewExecutionStore` and `NewQueue`.
- `driver/history_store.go`: `HistoryStore` now embeds the `p.HistoryBranchUtil` **interface** (constructed via `p.NewHistoryBranchUtil(serializer)`) instead of the old `p.HistoryBranchUtilImpl` value; added an explicit `GetHistoryBranchUtil()` accessor (required by `p.ExecutionStore`, no longer provided by the embedded type itself); simplified the two `h.GetHistoryBranchUtil().ParseHistoryBranchInfo(...)` call sites to `h.ParseHistoryBranchInfo(...)` directly, matching upstream's own equivalent diff.
- `driver/execution_store.go`, `mutable_state_store.go`, `mutable_state_task_store.go`: threaded `serializer serialization.Serializer` through constructors; fixed the four removed free-function call sites (`WorkflowExecutionStateToBlob/FromBlob`, `ReplicationTaskInfoToBlob`) to use the injected `d.serializer.*` methods.
- `driver/errors.go`: `exportCurrentWorkflowConflictError` is a free function with no store context, so its `WorkflowExecutionStateFromBlob` call became `serialization.DefaultDecoder.WorkflowExecutionStateFromBlob(...)` (matches upstream's identical fix in the Cassandra plugin).
- `integration/core/util.go`: the one non-test-file call site (`metaFactory.NewFactory(...)`) needed a `serialization.NewSerializer()` argument to keep the whole module (not just `driver/`) compiling — required regardless of the test-harness issue's own scope, since Go compiles all non-`_test.go` files in `go build ./...`.

**Deliberate deviation from the issue text:** the issue description (mirroring upstream's own Cassandra plugin) said `NewMutableStateStore` should also gain a `logger log.Logger` param. Skipped it: upstream needed the logger for a `softassert` warning when `ArchetypeID` is unspecified, as part of its sentinel-run-ID-encoding approach to CHASM separate ID spaces. Our design instead uses a dedicated `current_chasm_executions` table (see the CHASM section of this spec) and never needs to soft-assert on a zero `ArchetypeID` in the driver — `ExecutionManager` upstream already guarantees it's never zero on the wire. Adding an unused logger field would be dead weight. `i-1myt` (archetype routing) is free to add it later if some other need for logging surfaces there.

**Also deviated from upstream's own inconsistency, for the better:** upstream's Cassandra `QueueStore` keeps self-constructing `serialization.NewSerializer()` internally rather than accepting an injected one, even after the general injection refactor landed elsewhere. Chose full consistency here instead — `NewQueueStore` now takes an injected `serializer` too (4th param), threaded from `InstanceFactory.serializer`, and `convertQueueMetadata` takes the serializer as an explicit param instead of reaching for a package-level free function. This means every store in this driver now shares one process-wide serializer instance, matching the intent of the upstream refactor more completely than upstream's own reference implementation does.

**Evidence:**
- `go build ./...` — zero errors outside `cmd/server/main.go` (2 errors, both scoped to `i-5y8n`, unaffected by this issue).
- `go vet ./...` — zero errors outside the same `cmd/server/main.go` two errors plus `integration/core/integration_test.go`'s `NewExecutionMutableStateSuite` arg-count mismatch (scoped to `i-67u5`, which is correctly blocked on this issue and on `i-1myt`).
- `go vet ./driver/...` (including `driver/errors_test.go` and all driver unit tests) — clean, zero errors.
- `go vet` on every package except the two known-scoped ones — clean.

**Files touched:** `driver/factory.go`, `driver/history_store.go`, `driver/execution_store.go`, `driver/mutable_state_store.go`, `driver/mutable_state_task_store.go`, `driver/queue_store.go`, `driver/errors.go`, `integration/core/util.go`.

title: Add v1.2 schema migration (current_chasm_executions)
content:
Pure schema/DDL addition, no driver code: new `schema/yugabyte/temporal/versioned/v1.2/` with `current_chasm_executions` table (additive, no data migration) and matching `manifest.json`; bump `schema/yugabyte/version.go` `Version` to `"1.2"` (also fixes pre-existing staleness where it was left at `"1.0"`).

Full design: [[s-96n4]].

Blocked by the go.mod bump (no code dependency, but keep sequenced with the epic). Can run in parallel with the serializer injection work. Blocks [[i-chasm-routing]].

feedback.content:
**Implemented exactly per spec**, no deviations:
- `schema/yugabyte/temporal/versioned/v1.2/{manifest.json,schema.cql}` — additive `CREATE TABLE current_chasm_executions`, `MinCompatibleVersion: "1.0"`.
- `schema/yugabyte/version.go` `Version` bumped `"1.0"` → `"1.2"` (fixes the pre-existing staleness noted in the spec).
- Also added the table to `schema/yugabyte/temporal/create-schema.cql` / `drop-schema.cql` — these are the full-snapshot files `integration/core/cluster.go`'s `LoadSchema` actually uses for test setup (not the versioned migration path), so the integration suite needs the table there too, not just in the v1.2 migration.

**Evidence (live validation, not just DDL review):** spun up a standalone `yugabytedb/yugabyte:latest` container via Docker, built `cmd/tools/cassandra` at the new server version, and ran the real `create` → `setup-schema -v 0.0` → `update-schema -d ./schema/yugabyte/temporal/versioned` sequence (same as `make install-schema-yb`). Confirmed:
- Migration log shows `Schema Dirs: [v1.0 v1.1 v1.2]` and applies v1.0 → v1.1 → v1.2 in order, ending `Schema updated from 1.1 to 1.2`.
- `schema_version.curr_version` reads back `1.2`.
- `DESCRIBE TABLE current_chasm_executions` matches the spec's DDL exactly, including `PRIMARY KEY ((shard_id, namespace_id, workflow_id, archetype_id))`.
- Insert/select round-trip against the new table succeeds.

Container torn down after validation; no lasting infra changes.

title: Archetype-aware routing in mutable_state_store.go
content:
Branch every current-execution call site in `driver/mutable_state_store.go` on `request.ArchetypeID == chasm.WorkflowArchetypeID` to select between `current_executions` and the new `current_chasm_executions` table: `CreateWorkflowExecution`, `UpdateWorkflowExecution`, `ConflictResolveWorkflowExecution`, `DeleteCurrentWorkflowExecution`, `GetCurrentExecution`, and the three validator helpers (`validateCurrentWorkflowNotExist`/`validateCurrentWorkflowRunId`/`validateCurrentWorkflowMvcc`). Needs a second set of query template constants (mirror the `_v2` suffix convention from `matching_task_store_v2.go`).

Full design: [[s-96n4]].

Needs both the new table (schema migration issue) and the new `NewMutableStateStore(serializer, logger)` constructor signature (serializer injection issue) in place first. Validated by upstream's `TestArchetypeSeparateIDSpace`, pulled in transitively via the test-harness update.

feedback.content:
**Implemented per spec, with a cleaner helper design than originally sketched:**

Added 6 new query template constants (`templateUpdateCurrentChasmExecutionQuery(Prefix|ForNewQuery)`, `templateCreateCurrentChasmExecutionQuery`, `templateGetCurrentChasmExecutionQuery`, `templateGetCurrentChasmExecutionConflictQuery`, `templateDeleteCurrentChasmExecutionQuery`) mirroring the `current_executions` templates 1:1, targeting `current_chasm_executions` with an added `archetype_id` predicate/column.

Rather than branching on `archetypeID == chasm.WorkflowArchetypeID` inline at each of the ~10 call sites (as the issue text sketched), factored it into 7 small helpers: `currentExecutionUpdateForNewQuery`, `currentExecutionUpdateQuery`, `currentExecutionCreateQuery`, `currentExecutionGetQuery`, `currentExecutionGetConflictQuery`, `currentExecutionDeleteQuery` (each picks the workflow-or-chasm query template) and `currentExecutionKeyArgs` (returns the WHERE-clause key args: `(shardID, namespaceID, workflowID)` for a workflow, `(shardID, namespaceID, workflowID, archetypeID)` for any other archetype). This collapsed what would have been ~10 near-duplicate if/else blocks into single-line calls at each site and makes the archetype-routing decision testable/reviewable in one place instead of scattered inline.

Updated: `CreateWorkflowExecution` (both `UpdateCurrent` and `BrandNew` modes), `UpdateWorkflowExecution` (both sub-branches of `UpdateCurrent`), `ConflictResolveWorkflowExecution` (`UpdateCurrent` mode), `DeleteCurrentWorkflowExecution`, `GetCurrentExecution`, the three validator helpers (`validateCurrentWorkflowNotExist`/`validateCurrentWorkflowRunId`/`validateCurrentWorkflowMvcc`, each gained an `archetypeID chasm.ArchetypeID` parameter), and `assertNotCurrentExecution` (same). `request.ArchetypeID` is read once per method and threaded through.

**Confirmed out of scope, no changes needed:** `GetWorkflowExecution`, `DeleteWorkflowExecution`, `ListConcreteExecutions`, `SetWorkflowExecution`, and `decodeConflict` — none touch `current_executions`/`current_chasm_executions` (they key on `run_id` against the `executions` table, which is already globally unique, or don't touch current-record tables at all). `ListConcreteExecutions` in particular needs no "skip sentinel row" special-casing the way upstream's Cassandra plugin does, because this schema never stores a current-record marker inside `executions` itself.

**Evidence — this is the highest-risk change in the whole port (positional SQL args aren't statically checked against query text), so verified live, not just by compiling:**
- `go build ./...` fully clean across the whole module (first time since the version bump started).
- `go vet ./driver/...` clean; `go test ./driver/...` — all existing tests pass.
- Spun up a fresh YugabyteDB container, applied the full v1.0→v1.1→v1.2 schema via the real `cmd/tools/cassandra` tool, and ran a temporary live test (written and deleted after verification, not part of the permanent suite) directly against `driver.MetaFactory`/`ExecutionStore` — no test-suite scaffolding, no mocks:
  1. `CreateWorkflowExecution` with `ArchetypeID: chasm.WorkflowArchetypeID` and a second with `ArchetypeID: 424242`, **both sharing the identical `WorkflowID`** ("shared-business-id").
  2. `GetCurrentExecution` for each archetype independently returned its own distinct `RunID` — no collision.
  3. Raw CQL cross-check (`SELECT current_run_id FROM current_executions ...` vs `FROM current_chasm_executions ...`) confirmed the two rows physically landed in the correct separate tables with the correct `run_id` in each.
  4. `DeleteCurrentWorkflowExecution` on the CHASM entity removed only its row; the workflow's current record was confirmed unaffected afterward.
  5. Ran 4 times total, consistently passing.

This is exactly the scenario upstream's `TestArchetypeSeparateIDSpace` (in `common/persistence/tests/execution_mutable_state.go`) checks, run manually since that suite isn't reachable yet (blocked on `i-67u5`). Once the test harness issue lands and the full `commontests.NewExecutionMutableStateSuite` becomes runnable, `TestArchetypeSeparateIDSpace` will re-confirm this same behavior as part of the permanent suite.

**Files touched:** `driver/mutable_state_store.go` only.

title: ClusterMember.HostID to []byte plus ConvertError/RequestErrWriteTimeout parity
content:
In `driver/cluster_metadata_store.go`: change `ClusterMember.HostID`, `GetClusterMembersRequest.HostIDEquals`, `UpsertClusterMembershipRequest.HostID` from `uuid.UUID` to `[]byte`; drop the `github.com/pborman/uuid` import and now-unnecessary conversions; change the `HostIDEquals != nil` check to `len(...) != 0`.

Also port two upstream correctness fixes into this project's forked `utils/gocql/errors.go`: match `*gocql.RequestErrWriteTimeout` as a pointer type in `errors.As`, and add a `*serviceerror.ResourceExhausted` passthrough to `ConvertError`.

Full design: [[s-88l3]]. Independent of the serializer/CHASM work; can run in parallel. Blocked only by the go.mod bump.

feedback.content:
**Implemented exactly per spec, plus one added regression test:**
- `driver/cluster_metadata_store.go`: `ClusterMember.HostID`, `GetClusterMembersRequest.HostIDEquals`, `UpsertClusterMembershipRequest.HostID` are now `[]byte` end to end; dropped the `github.com/pborman/uuid` import and both now-unnecessary conversions (`uuid.UUID(cqlHostID)` on read, `[]byte(request.HostID)` on write — the values were already `[]byte`); `HostIDEquals != nil` → `len(request.HostIDEquals) != 0`.
- `utils/gocql/errors.go`: `var cqlTimeoutErr gocql.RequestErrWriteTimeout` → `*gocql.RequestErrWriteTimeout` (pointer). Added a `*serviceerror.ResourceExhausted` passthrough via the new stdlib `errors.AsType[T]` generic (confirmed this Go 1.26.4 toolchain has it — it's genuinely new in the stdlib, not a Temporal-internal helper).
- `go.mod`/`go.sum`: `github.com/pborman/uuid` fully dropped via `go mod tidy` — nothing else in the repo referenced it.

**Found and fixed a latent, pre-existing bug while doing this** (not introduced by the version bump, but directly in scope for "RequestErrWriteTimeout parity"): the old `var cqlTimeoutErr gocql.RequestErrWriteTimeout` (value type) could never actually match via `errors.As`, because `github.com/yugabyte/gocql`'s `frame.go` always constructs and returns `&RequestErrWriteTimeout{...}` (a pointer). So write-timeout errors were silently falling through to the generic `serviceerror.NewUnavailable(...)` branch instead of being classified as `persistence.TimeoutError` — meaning callers never got the deterministic-retry signal a `TimeoutError` provides. This was true before v1.29.7 too; the upstream diff just happened to surface it. Fixed by matching upstream's fix (pointer type).

**Evidence:**
- Added `utils/gocql/errors_test.go` with two new tests (no test coverage existed for `ConvertError` before): `TestConvertError_RequestErrWriteTimeout` constructs a real `&gocql.RequestErrWriteTimeout{}` and asserts `ConvertError` returns a `*persistence.TimeoutError` (would have failed under the pre-fix value-type code — confirmed by inspecting `errors.As`'s exact-type-match semantics against the pointer-constructing driver code). `TestConvertError_ResourceExhaustedPassthrough` wraps a `*serviceerror.ResourceExhausted` and asserts it comes back unchanged (`require.Same`). Both pass.
- `go test ./driver/... ./utils/...` — all existing tests still pass.
- `go build ./...` — zero errors outside `cmd/server/main.go` (scoped to `i-5y8n`).
- `go vet` on every package except `cmd/server`/`integration/core` (the two known-scoped exceptions) — clean.
- `go mod tidy` — clean, confirms `pborman/uuid` had no other references.

**Files touched:** `driver/cluster_metadata_store.go`, `utils/gocql/errors.go`, new `utils/gocql/errors_test.go`, `go.mod`/`go.sum`.

title: CompleteHistoryTask honors BestEffort
content:
In `driver/mutable_state_task_store.go`, add `if request.BestEffort { return nil }` as the first line of `CompleteHistoryTask`, matching upstream's Cassandra store. Safe minimum — defers real best-effort semantics to a later pass.

Full design: [[s-88l3]]. Independent, one-line change; can run in parallel. Blocked only by the go.mod bump.

feedback.content:
**Implemented exactly per spec, no deviations:** added `if request.BestEffort { return nil }` as the first line of `MutableStateTaskStore.CompleteHistoryTask` in `driver/mutable_state_task_store.go`, byte-for-byte matching upstream's Cassandra store fix.

**Evidence:** added `driver/mutable_state_task_store_test.go` with `TestCompleteHistoryTask_BestEffort`, which calls the method on a zero-value `&MutableStateTaskStore{}` (nil `Session`) with `BestEffort: true` — this only passes because the guard short-circuits before any session/category access; a nil-pointer panic would result if the guard weren't unconditionally first. No prior unit coverage existed for this store at the `driver` package level (everything else is validated only through the full integration suite against live YugabyteDB), so this is net-new coverage, not a modification of an existing test.

Checked upstream's own `common/persistence/tests/execution_mutable_state_task.go` (the suite this project pulls in via `commontests.NewExecutionMutableStateTaskSuite`) for `BestEffort`-specific assertions — none exist yet upstream either, consistent with `EnableBestEffortDeleteTasksOnWorkflowUpdate` defaulting to `false`. Real end-to-end behavior (does a best-effort delete actually get silently dropped in a live workflow-update path) is exercised transitively once `history.enableBestEffortDeleteTasksOnWorkflowUpdate` is turned on and the full integration suite runs — covered by the final Verify issue, not unit-testable in isolation beyond what's added here.

`go build ./...` / `go vet ./driver/...` / `go test ./driver/...` all clean.

**Files touched:** `driver/mutable_state_task_store.go`, new `driver/mutable_state_task_store_test.go`.

title: Update cmd/server/main.go to renamed upstream APIs
content:
This file is a full fork of upstream's `cmd/server/main.go` and must track its renames: `config.LoadConfig(env, dir, zone)` → `config.Load(config.WithEnv(env), config.WithConfigDir(dir), config.WithZone(zone))` (consider also wiring the new `--config-file` flag / `config.WithConfigFile` / `config.WithEmbedded` paths to stay a faithful fork); `dynamicconfig.ValidateFile` → `dynamicconfig.LoadYamlFile`; `tag.NewStringTag/NewTimeTag/NewBoolTag` → `tag.String/Time/Bool`; remove the manual `dynamicconfig.NewFileBasedClient`/`NewNoopClient` construction and `temporal.WithDynamicConfigClient(...)` call since `temporal.NewServer` now derives it from `cfg.DynamicConfigClient` internally.

Full design: [[s-88l3]]. Independent; can run in parallel. Blocked only by the go.mod bump.

feedback.content:
**Implemented per spec, plus the invited `--config-file` addition:**
- `config.LoadConfig(env, configDir, zone)` → `config.Load(config.WithEnv(env), config.WithConfigDir(configDir), config.WithZone(zone))`.
- `dynamicconfig.ValidateFile` → `dynamicconfig.LoadYamlFile`.
- `tag.NewStringTag/NewTimeTag/NewBoolTag` → `tag.String/Time/Bool` (6 call sites in the build-info log line).
- Removed the manual `dynamicConfigClient` construction (`dynamicconfig.NewFileBasedClient`/`NewNoopClient`) and the `temporal.WithDynamicConfigClient(...)` call — verified against upstream's `temporal/fx.go` `serverOptionsProvider`: it now derives `dcClient` from `so.config.DynamicConfigClient` automatically (falling back to a noop client) whenever `WithDynamicConfigClient` wasn't explicitly set, so the old manual code was fully redundant.
- Added the `--config-file` flag and the three-way `switch` (`--config-file` / `--config`+`--env`+`--zone` / embedded-default) matching upstream's own `cmd/server/main.go` exactly, per the issue's invitation to "stay a faithful fork." Added the matching `Before`-hook mutual-exclusivity check (`--config-file` can't combine with `--config`/`--env`/`--zone`/`--root`).
- Updated the four flag `Usage` strings to append `(deprecated)`, matching upstream's own wording — purely cosmetic, zero behavior change.

**Deliberately NOT ported** (confirmed pre-existing, unrelated to this version bump): upstream's `cmd/server/main.go` at v1.31.2 also has a `render-config` command and audience-mapper wiring (`GetAudienceMapperFromConfig`/`WithAudienceGetter`) that this project's fork has never had — checked upstream's `v1.29.7` tag and both were already present there too, so their absence here is a pre-existing gap unrelated to the 1.29.7→1.31.2 breakage, not something this issue's "renamed APIs" scope covers. Left untouched.

**Evidence — real binary, not just compile:**
- `go build ./...` — zero errors across the whole module (previously the only 2 remaining errors were both in this file).
- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /tmp/temporal-server-test ./cmd/server` succeeds; `--version` reports `1.31.2`; `--help` shows the new `--config-file` flag and `(deprecated)` wording.
- `validate-dynamic-config docker/config/dynamicconfig/docker.yaml` exits 0 with no warnings/errors — confirms `dynamicconfig.LoadYamlFile` works against a real project config file.
- `--env development --allow-no-auth start` against `config/development.yaml`: confirmed via structured JSON logs that config loading, the renamed `tag.*` build-info log line (correct git-revision/go-arch/server-version=1.31.2/etc.), authorizer/claim-mapper wiring, and — most importantly — the **automatic dynamic-config-client derivation** all work correctly (dozens of "dynamic config changed for the key: ..." log lines fire automatically from the fx-internal wiring, proving `cfg.DynamicConfigClient` is picked up without any manual `WithDynamicConfigClient` call). It proceeds through the full `temporal.NewServer`/fx bootstrap and only stops with a `logger.Fatal` (not a panic/crash) at `driver.MetaFactory.NewFactory` when it can't dial YugabyteDB on `127.0.0.1:9042` — expected and correct, since no live datastore is running in this environment. Getting a fully-serving instance up requires Elasticsearch too and real schema application, which is the final Verify issue's job (`i-6r6q`), not re-done here.
- `go vet ./cmd/...` and `gofmt -l cmd/server/main.go` both clean.

**Files touched:** `cmd/server/main.go` only.

title: Update integration/core test harness call sites
content:
Update `integration/core/integration_test.go` call sites to the new upstream `common/persistence/tests` suite constructor signatures — in particular `commontests.NewExecutionMutableStateSuite` drops the `historyBranchUtil` parameter entirely (was `(t, shardStore, executionStore, serializer, historyBranchUtil, logger)`, now `(t, shardStore, executionStore, serializer, logger)`). Confirm `driver/queue_v2_store.go`'s use of `serialization.NewUnknownEncodingTypeError`/`NewDeserializationError` is unaffected (those free functions didn't move).

Full design: [[s-28q1]]. Must land after the driver-side signature changes it exercises — blocked by both the serializer injection issue and the archetype-routing issue (the suite it drives includes `TestArchetypeSeparateIDSpace`).

feedback.content:
**Implemented exactly per spec — a true one-line fix:** removed the `&persistence.HistoryBranchUtilImpl{}` argument from the `commontests.NewExecutionMutableStateSuite(...)` call in `integration/core/integration_test.go`, matching the new 5-arg upstream signature. Confirmed `driver/queue_v2_store.go`'s `serialization.NewUnknownEncodingTypeError`/`NewDeserializationError` usages are untouched free functions, exactly as the issue anticipated — no change needed there.

**Evidence — went well beyond compiling, ran the real suites against live infrastructure:**
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are now **fully clean across the entire module** — the first time in this whole port. Every prior wave-2/wave-3 issue's "clean except for X, scoped to issue Y" note is now resolved.
- Spun up a fresh YugabyteDB container, applied the full schema, and ran `TestYugabyteExecutionMutableStateStoreSuite` for real: **all 37 subtests pass**, including `TestArchetypeSeparateIDSpace` and every new CHASM-specific test (`TestCreate_BrandNew_CHASM`, `TestCreate_Reuse_CHASM`, `TestSet_CHASM`, `TestUpdate_NotZombie_CHASM`, `TestConflictResolve_SuppressCurrent_WithNew_CHASM`) — this is the upstream test [[i-1myt]]'s work was designed to satisfy, now confirmed via the real suite rather than my own hand-rolled verification. `TestListConcreteExecutions` correctly SKIPs with "only implemented by cassandra persistence" (pre-existing, intentional, unrelated to this port).
- Went further and ran the **entire** `TestYugabyte*` suite set (all 15 suites in the file — Shard, ExecutionMutableState(+Task), History(V2), TaskQueue(+Fair/Task/UserData), ClusterMetadataPersistence, QueuePersistence, NexusEndpointPersistence, QueueV2Persistence): 13 of 15 fully pass, confirming no regressions anywhere else in the port (including [[i-4dgp]]'s `HostID []byte` change, exercised directly by `TestYugabyteClusterMetadataPersistence`).
- **Found 2 new failures in `TestYugabyteMetadataPersistenceV2`** (`driver/metadata_store.go`, untouched by any issue in this epic). Confirmed via upstream diff that both are brand-new test cases added at v1.31.2 — not a regression, but a real gap this version bump newly exercises. Filed as [[i-405w]] (`discovered-from` this issue, blocks the final Verify issue) rather than fixed here, since it's a different file/component outside this issue's stated scope.

title: Verify: build, schema apply, integration + Clojure e2e, manual smoke test
content:
Run the full acceptance criteria from [[s-2kt2]]: `go build`/`go vet`, apply the v1.2 schema migration via `make install-schema-yb`, run the Go integration suite (`integration/core`) including the new `TestArchetypeSeparateIDSpace`, run the Clojure e2e suite (`integration/clojure`), and do a manual smoke test per the README dev flow. Closing this issue is the exit criterion for the whole epic.

Blocked by every other issue in this epic.

feedback.content:
**All 5 acceptance criteria verified against real infrastructure. The epic is done.**

**1. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass** — confirmed clean, as they have been since [[i-67u5]] closed.

**2. Schema applies cleanly (v1.0→v1.1→v1.2→v1.3), `schema/yugabyte/version.go` matches.**
Built the real `make bin` artifacts (`target/temporal-server`, `target/temporal-cassandra-tool`, `target/temporal`) and ran the exact `install-schema-yb`/`integration/run.sh` sequence (`create` → `setup-schema -v 0.0` → `update-schema -d ./schema/yugabyte/temporal/versioned`) against a fresh YugabyteDB container. Log confirms `Schema updated from 1.0 to 1.1` → `1.1 to 1.2` → `1.2 to 1.3`, ending at version `1.3` — matching `schema/yugabyte/version.go`.

**3. Go integration suite passes, including `TestArchetypeSeparateIDSpace`.**
Already fully verified in [[i-67u5]] and [[i-405w]]: all 15 `TestYugabyte*` suites pass with zero failures (re-confirmed once more this session as part of the schema/build validation above, no new failures).

**4. Clojure e2e suite confirms real workflow execution.**
Built the uberjar (`lein uberjar`, 31 test namespaces compiled clean) and ran it against a fully live stack: YugabyteDB + Elasticsearch (via `docker/docker-compose/integrate.yml`, the same compose file CI uses) + the actual `temporal-server` binary (`--env development --allow-no-auth start`) + a real `default` namespace created via the `temporal` CLI. **First run against fresh state: 31 tests, 44 steps, 50 assertions, 31 pass, 0 errors** — covering activities, child workflows, signals, queries, retries, timeouts, side effects, sequencing, concurrency/race, heartbeats, local activities, and reuse-policy semantics. This is genuine end-to-end proof that workflow start/signal/query/complete work correctly against the ported driver.

Re-ran a second time out of extra caution: got 30 pass / 1 error, but the one error (`reuse-policy` test's fixed workflow ID colliding with a *completed* execution left over from the first run, `WorkflowExecutionAlreadyStarted`) is a **test-fixture artifact of reusing the same persisted namespace across two manual invocations**, not a driver defect — the test uses a hardcoded workflow ID with `reject-duplicate` reuse policy, which is *correctly* rejecting a duplicate against my own leftover state. In the real CI usage pattern (`integration/run.sh`), a fresh YugabyteDB+ES is provisioned per run, so this never recurs. The clean first-run result is the valid signal.

**5. Manual smoke test per the README dev flow.**
Went beyond the documented flow's minimum: `cluster health` reported `SERVING`, `namespace create` succeeded via the real CLI, and the server log showed the `temporal-sys-history-scanner-workflow` system workflow starting successfully on its own — proof the full persistence stack (shards, tasks, history, matching, visibility) is live end-to-end, not just reachable. One CLI nuance noted for anyone following the README: `./target/temporal operator ...` needs an explicit `--address 127.0.0.1:7233` when run outside its own default resolution path — a `temporalio/cli` behavior, not something this port changed, and not worth fixing here.

**One deviation worth flagging for whoever deploys this next:** `config/integration.yaml` hardcodes Docker-network hostnames (`yugabyte`, `elasticsearch`) that only resolve inside the `integration-test` compose network. Running the stack host-side (as I did here, and as anyone doing local manual verification would) requires either `/etc/hosts` entries or, more simply, using `--env development` instead (which already points at `127.0.0.1` and is what I used). This is pre-existing, unrelated to this port.

Full cleanup performed: server process killed, `docker compose down` removed both containers and the network, temp logs deleted. `git status` shows only the files already recorded in [[i-405w]]'s feedback — this issue made no additional code changes, pure verification.

**The epic's full acceptance criteria are met. All 9 planned issues plus the 1 discovered issue are closed.**

title: MetadataStore fails 2 new v1.31.2 persistence-suite tests
content:
Discovered while validating [[i-67u5]]: running the full `integration/core` suite against a live YugabyteDB (all 15 `TestYugabyte*` suites) surfaces 2 failures in `TestYugabyteMetadataPersistenceV2`, both against `driver/metadata_store.go`, a file no issue in this epic touches.

Confirmed via `git diff v1.29.7..v1.31.2 -- common/persistence/persistence-tests/metadata_persistence_v2.go` that **both are brand-new test cases added at v1.31.2** — they never existed at v1.29.7, so this isn't a regression from anything changed in this epic; it's a pre-existing gap in `driver/metadata_store.go` that nothing exercised until now.

## 1. `TestCreateNamespaceWithDuplicateID` — likely a real bug

Creates namespace A with `id=X, name="name1"`, then creates namespace B with `id=X` (same ID) but `name="name2"` (different name). Expects the second `CreateNamespace` to fail with `*serviceerror.NamespaceAlreadyExists`; our driver returns `nil` (succeeds).

Root cause (confirmed by reading `driver/metadata_store.go:96` `CreateNamespace`): the CAS conflict check is `INSERT INTO namespaces (name, id, ...) ... IF NOT EXISTS`, which is scoped to the `namespaces` table's partition key (`name`). Since `name2` doesn't exist yet, the `IF NOT EXISTS` check passes even though `id=X` already exists under `name1`. `namespace_by_id_idx` is a secondary index, and secondary indexes never enforce uniqueness in Cassandra/YCQL — so duplicate-ID detection needs an explicit check (e.g. a lookup via `namespace_by_id_idx` before/inside the same transaction, or a dedicated `namespaces_by_id` table with its own `IF NOT EXISTS`, similar to the two-table pattern `CreateNamespaceInV2Table` already partially uses for namespace metadata versioning).

## 2. `TestRenameNamespaceCassandra` — likely NOT a bug, needs a judgment call

Test explicitly pins a **Cassandra-specific quirk**: renaming a namespace to its own current name is expected to fail with `*serviceerror.Unavailable`, because Cassandra's `RenameNamespace` uses a two-step `INSERT ... IF NOT EXISTS` where the second step's target row already exists. The test's own comment says: "In Cassandra, this will fail... which is expected behavior for Cassandra's two-step process."

This project's entire stated design purpose (see README "Differences from the original code") is replacing Cassandra's LWT/`IF NOT EXISTS` batch patterns with real YCQL distributed transactions specifically to avoid this class of quirk. It's plausible our `RenameNamespace` handles rename-to-same-name gracefully (a no-op success) rather than failing — which would be *better* behavior, not a bug, but it means this specific test's assumption doesn't hold for a non-Cassandra-shaped backend.

**Decision needed:** either (a) confirm our `RenameNamespace` genuinely no-ops correctly on same-name rename and exclude this Cassandra-specific test the same way `TestRenameNamespaceSQL` is already skipped for this suite, or (b) if our driver actually errors here too but with the wrong error type/for a different reason, fix it to match.

## Scope note

Not fixed as part of [[i-67u5]] (which was specifically about the `historyBranchUtil` call-site removal, already verified independently) or [[i-1myt]] (archetype routing, unrelated file). This blocks [[i-6r6q]]'s acceptance criterion that "all previously-passing suites... still pass" only in the sense that the *full* suite must be green before the epic can close — these 2 tests were never run before, so nothing regressed, but they must be resolved (fixed or deliberately excluded with justification) before Verify can close cleanly.

feedback.content:
**Both failures resolved — one real fix, one justified exclusion, exactly as the issue's judgment call anticipated:**

**1. `TestCreateNamespaceWithDuplicateID` — fixed with a new schema table (v1.3).**

Confirmed root cause: `namespaces`' PK is `name`; `id` is only a secondary index (`namespace_by_id_idx`), which never enforces uniqueness in YCQL. Added `namespaces_by_id` (PK `id`) so ID uniqueness is atomically checked via its own `IF NOT EXISTS`, participating in the *same* distributed transaction as every write to `namespaces` — no orphan-cleanup dance needed (unlike upstream Cassandra's batch+cleanup two-table approach), since this driver's transactions are real ACID, not conditional batches.
- `schema/yugabyte/temporal/versioned/v1.3/{manifest.json,schema.cql}` — additive `CREATE TABLE namespaces_by_id`.
- `schema/yugabyte/version.go` bumped `"1.2"` → `"1.3"`; added to `create-schema.cql`/`drop-schema.cql` (the full-snapshot files the test harness actually loads).
- `driver/metadata_store.go`: `CreateNamespace` now also inserts into `namespaces_by_id` in the same txn (the existing `gocql.ConflictError(err) → NewNamespaceAlreadyExists` catch-all needed no changes — it already covers a conflict on *either* table). `RenameNamespace` updates the cached `name` in `namespaces_by_id` (id doesn't change, no uniqueness risk, plain `UPDATE`). `DeleteNamespace`/`DeleteNamespaceByName` both now also delete the `namespaces_by_id` row (the latter needed a new `id`-by-`name` lookup first, since it's only given a name) — added to keep the new table's invariant ("`namespaces_by_id` mirrors `namespaces` 1:1 while a namespace exists") from drifting after rename/delete, matching the level of care upstream's own by-id table takes.

**2. `TestRenameNamespaceCassandra` — confirmed NOT a bug, excluded via suite-method override.**

Verified: this driver's `RenameNamespace` genuinely succeeds when renaming to the same name — YugabyteDB's real distributed transactions give it sequential consistency within the same `BEGIN/END TRANSACTION` (the DELETE removes the row, then the INSERT's `IF NOT EXISTS` correctly sees it already gone), unlike Cassandra's conditional-batch statements which are all evaluated against one pre-batch snapshot. This is intentionally better behavior, not a regression — exactly matching this project's stated design purpose (README: replacing Cassandra's LWT/batch quirks with real transactions).

The test itself only self-skips for `*sql.TestCluster` (a binary SQL-vs-Cassandra assumption baked into the upstream suite that doesn't account for a third backend), so it can't skip itself for us. Added a thin wrapper type `yugabyteMetadataPersistenceSuiteV2` in `integration/core/integration_test.go` that embeds `*persistencetests.MetadataPersistenceSuiteV2` and shadows just `TestRenameNamespaceCassandra()` with `s.T().Skip(...)` — Go method-shadowing via embedding, so every other test (including `TestRenameNamespaceWithNameConflict`, `TestCASFailureUpdateNamespace`, etc.) still runs unmodified via promoted methods. Same mechanism `TestRenameNamespaceSQL` already gets for free, just applied manually since upstream's type-switch doesn't cover us.

**Evidence:**
- `go build ./...` / `go vet ./...` fully clean.
- Live run: **all 22 subtests in `TestYugabyteMetadataPersistenceV2` pass or correctly skip** (`TestRenameNamespaceCassandra` and `TestRenameNamespaceSQL` both SKIP, everything else PASS) — including the partial-namespace edge cases (`TestCreateWithPartialNamespaceDifferentNameSameID`/`SameNameDifferentID`/`SameNameSameID`) and `TestInitializeSystemNamespaces`, confirming the new delete/rename sync logic doesn't break existing lifecycle paths.
- Re-ran the **entire 15-suite `TestYugabyte*` battery**: **all 15 pass, zero failures** — this is the first fully green run of the complete integration test suite in this whole port.

**Files touched:** `driver/metadata_store.go`, `integration/core/integration_test.go`, `schema/yugabyte/version.go`, `schema/yugabyte/temporal/{create-schema.cql,drop-schema.cql}`, new `schema/yugabyte/temporal/versioned/v1.3/`.
